waivers.author: solution-author
waivers.authorJustification: This check is a roll-up of the evidence sections. Six sections passed with real lab evidence (alert lifecycle, deployment and readback, image rendering, mock ingestion, UI traversal with 45/45 portal query-executor responses HTTP 200, workbook queries 17/17 identical on Log Analytics and Advanced Hunting). It fails only because of three sections that are individually waived with documented evidence in this file: alertParity (E2E-Q03: tactics and entities differ), dataConnectorIngestion (QUAL-DC-01: third-party sources unavailable in the lab) and urlVerification (QUAL-URL-01: two non-link URL strings). It adds no independent failure.

waivers.author: solution-author
waivers.authorJustification: Live alert parity ran on both surfaces for both detections with real mock data: each Analytic Rule and its Custom Detection raised exactly 1 alert, with identical match keys (198.51.100.10 and 198.51.100.20), severity and evidence. Five of seven strict-parity dimensions pass (alertCount, matchKeys, expectedMatches, severity, evidence); all rules and detections were restored to disabled afterwards. Two dimensions do NOT match and are not claimed to: (1) tactics - the Analytic Rules declare two tactics each (Execution+Impact; Impact+DefenseEvasion) while the packaged Custom Detection carries one (V3.1 single-tactic projection of the Custom Detection schema; the omitted tactic is recorded in the packaging log); (2) entities - the Analytic Rules map the plain user name (DstUserName) to an Account entity, while the Custom Detection account mapping requires a UPN or SID, so the converter omits the account mapping; the host/IP/file-hash evidence is equal. A reviewer must decide whether this functional difference is acceptable.

waivers.author: solution-author
waivers.authorJustification: Connector operation was NOT demonstrated and this waiver does not claim it was. All 45 sampleQueries/connectivityCriteria/lastDataReceivedQuery entries of the 4 packaged connectors were run verbatim, live, on Sentinel Log Analytics and Defender Advanced Hunting: 32 failed because the connector-created tables do not exist in the lab workspace, 12 ran with 0 rows and 1 returned 1 row. The lab has no CrowdStrike tenant, AWS S3/SQS or Falcon API credentials, so these connectors cannot be deployed or fed there. The migration did not modify any connector definition; the Function App deployment, authentication, pagination and invocation-log criteria were not performed. A reviewer must decide whether this lab limitation is acceptable.

waivers.author: solution-author
waivers.authorJustification: Browser verification opened 64 URLs; 62 returned success. The 2 failures are not documentation or logo links: (1) https://api.us-2.crowdstrike.com is the default CrowdStrike Falcon REST API base URL embedded in the package; it answers HTTP 404 at '/' because the API only serves versioned authenticated paths (the host is reachable, there is no landing page). (2) 'https://sqs' is a prefix of the format hint 'https://sqs.<region>.amazonaws.com/<12-digit-account-id>/<queue-name>' in the tooltip of Data Connectors/CrowdstrikeReplicatorCLv2/CSFDRv2_Deploymnet/createUiDefinition_csfdrv2_connector.json, where the user supplies their own AWS SQS queue URL; it is a template, not a link, and is not resolvable by design.

waivers.author: solution-author
waivers.authorJustification: The reported insecure-HTTP hits are format-mandated namespace/schema identifiers, not navigable links: the SVG xmlns in Data Connectors/Logo/crowdstrike.svg, the ARM $schema in Data Connectors/CrowdStrikeFalconAdversaryIntelligence/azure_deploy_CrowdstrikeFalconIndicatorsofCompromise.json and the Azure Functions $schema in Data Connectors/CrowdstrikeReplicatorCLv2/CrowdstrikeFalconAPISentinelConn/proxies.json. All three files are unchanged from upstream. The check reports a fourth hit that is the qualifier's own previous report under Evidence/pr-qualification quoting these same identifiers (self-referential, no additional URL exists in the solution). All 102 aka.ms links and the documentation/logo links were checked.

waivers.author: solution-author
waivers.authorJustification: The flagged files are not Sentinel data connector definitions and therefore legitimately lack connector id/title/dataTypes/instructionSteps: Azure Function App runtime files (host.json, proxies.json, function.json, EventsToTableMapping.json, RequiredFieldsSchema.json), custom/normalized table and DCR transformation artifacts, and a standalone deployment UI definition. The actual connector definition files were not flagged. No connector file was modified by the migration other than placeholder text in the standalone deployment UI definition (recorded in decision-manifest acknowledged_exclusions).
